summary: Repeatedly halve a monotonic search space by comparing the midpoint against a condition, discarding the half that cannot contain the answer, to find a target or boundary in logarithmic time.
recognize_when: The input is sorted, or the answer space is monotonic even if the input array isn't (binary search on the answer)
You need to find an exact value, insertion point, or boundary (first/last occurrence) faster than O(n)
The problem asks to minimize/maximize a value subject to a feasibility check that gets easier or harder monotonically (e.g. 'minimum capacity to ship in D days')
Constraints mention array sizes up to 10^5-10^7 with an expected O(log n) or O(n log n) solution
Searching in a rotated sorted array or a 2D matrix sorted row-wise and column-wise

complexity.notes: Each iteration eliminates half the remaining search space; iterative implementation needs no extra memory (recursive would add O(log n) call-stack space).

gotchas: Using (left + right) // 2 instead of left + (right - left) // 2, which can overflow in other languages and is worth the habit in Python too
Infinite loops from an incorrect boundary update (e.g. right = mid instead of right = mid - 1) when searching for a boundary rather than an exact match
Applying binary search to an array that isn't actually sorted/monotonic in the property being tested
examples: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
